title: Purity along a fibre descends under pointed flat base change
statement: Let $f:X\to S$ be a finite type morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-finite-type-morphism], and $F$ a finite type quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_X$-module [pqf-def-coherent, def-weil-pbc-module-finite-type-presentation]. Let $e:S^{\prime}\to S$, $s^{\prime}\in S^{\prime}$, and $s=e(s^{\prime})$. Suppose $e$ is flat at $s^{\prime}$, meaning that the map $\mathcal O_{S,s}\to\mathcal O_{S^{\prime},s^{\prime}}$ makes the latter a flat module [def-weil-flat-morphism]. Put $Y=X\times_SS^{\prime}$ [def-pc-fibre-product] and $F_Y=\operatorname{pr}_X^*F$ [def-pc-module-pullback]. If $F_Y$ is pure along $Y_{s^{\prime}}$, then $F$ is pure along $X_s$ [def-sfb-scheme-relative-purity, def-pc-scheme-fibre]. No residue-field isomorphism and no Noetherian hypothesis is required.

proof.text: Argue by contradiction. If $F$ is not pure along $X_s$, the definition gives an impurity $(v:T\to S,t'\leadsto t,\xi)$ with $(T,t)\to(S,s)$ elementary etale. Thus $v(t)=s$, $\kappa(s)\to\kappa(t)$ is an isomorphism, $\xi\in\operatorname{Ass}_{X_T/T}(F_T)$ lies over $t'$, and $\overline{\{\xi\}}\cap(X_T)_t=\varnothing$. The finite-type base-change lemma and the two pullback lemmas show that $X_T\to T$ is finite type and $F_T$ is finite type and quasi-coherent; they give the same properties after further base change to $T_1=T\times_SS'$.

source.place: Tag 05J9, lemma-flat-descend-pure, proof of (1) by lifting an elementary-etale impurity.

proof.text: Put $K=\kappa(s')$. The isomorphism $\kappa(s)\to\kappa(t)$ supplies a compatible field map $\kappa(t)\to K$. The field-valued-point lemma gives a morphism $\operatorname{Spec}K\to T$ over $S$; pair it with the canonical $\operatorname{Spec}K\to S'$ to obtain $a:\operatorname{Spec}K\to T_1$ by the fibre-product universal property. Its image $t_1$ maps to $t$ and $s'$. The induced maps $K\to\kappa(t_1)\to K$ compose to the identity, because the projection of $a$ is the canonical point of $S'$. The second map is injective, and its image contains $K$, so both maps are inverse isomorphisms. Also $T_1\to S'$ is etale by etale base change. Hence $(T_1,t_1)\to(S',s')$ is an elementary etale neighbourhood. Only $\kappa(t)=\kappa(s)$ from the chosen neighbourhood was used; no isomorphism $\kappa(s)\to\kappa(s')$ was assumed.

source.place: Tag 05J9, lemma-flat-descend-pure, proof of (1) by lifting an elementary-etale impurity.

proof.text: Write $h:T_1\to T$ for the other projection. Apply clause (1) of pointwise module-flatness base change to $e:S'\to S$, the quasi-coherent module $\mathcal O_{S'}$, the base change $T\to S$, and the point $t_1$ above $s'$. The hypothesis is exactly the stipulated flatness of $e$ at $s'$. Since, for $b:T_1\to S\prime$, $b^*\mathcal O_{S\prime}=\mathcal O_{T_1}\otimes_{b^{-1}\mathcal O_{S\prime}}b^{-1}\mathcal O_{S\prime}\cong\mathcal O_{T_1}$ by multiplication, its conclusion says $\mathcal O_{T_1,t_1}$ is flat over $\mathcal O_{T,t}$. Thus $h$ is flat at $t_1$.

source.place: Tag 05J9, lemma-flat-descend-pure, proof of (1) by lifting an elementary-etale impurity.

proof.text: Here is the local reduction needed to lift $t'\leadsto t$, so global flatness of $h$ is unnecessary. Set $A=\mathcal O_{T,t}$ and $B=\mathcal O_{T_1,t_1}$. The map $A\to B$ is local and flat, hence $\operatorname{Spec}B\to\operatorname{Spec}A$ is a flat morphism by the affine flatness equivalence. The canonical-local-spectrum lemma supplies a point $p\in\operatorname{Spec}A$ mapping to $t'$, since $t'$ generalizes $t$. Every prime of the local ring $A$ generalizes its closed point. Apply flat generalization lifting at the closed point of $\operatorname{Spec}B$, whose image is the closed point of $\operatorname{Spec}A$, to obtain $q$ over $p$. The canonical map $\operatorname{Spec}B\to T_1$ sends $q$ to $t_1'$ with $t_1'\leadsto t_1$. The local-spectrum square commutes (both maps on each affine neighbourhood are induced by the germ maps and $A\to B$), so $h(t_1')=t'$.

source.place: Tag 05J9, lemma-flat-descend-pure, proof of (1) by lifting an elementary-etale impurity.

proof.text: The ring $R=\kappa(t_1')\otimes_{\kappa(t')}\kappa(\xi)$ is nontrivial, since its two factors are field extensions of $\kappa(t')$. The maximal-ideal lemma makes $\operatorname{Spec}R$ nonempty. Choose a point of this spectrum, an irreducible component containing it by the component-cover lemma, and the generic point of that component by scheme sobriety. The fibre-product-points lemma, applied to $X_T\to T$ and $T_1\to T$, identifies this point with a point $\xi_1\in X_{T_1}$ over both $\xi$ and $t_1'$. In particular it is generic in an irreducible component of the residual fibre $\operatorname{Spec}R$.

source.place: Tag 05J9, lemma-flat-descend-pure, proof of (1) by lifting an elementary-etale impurity.

proof.text: Apply relative-assassin base change to $X_T\to T$, its quasi-coherent module $F_T$, and $T_1\to T$. Its locally-finite-type hypothesis follows from step 1, and $\xi$ is relative associated by the chosen impurity. The residual generic-point condition is precisely step 5. The stated equivalence therefore gives $\xi_1\in\operatorname{Ass}_{X_{T_1}/T_1}(F_{T_1})$. Pullback composition identifies this module with the pullback of $F_Y$ to $Y\times_{S'}T_1=X_{T_1}$; the identification of the schemes is the unique one commuting with their projections, by the fibre-product universal property.

source.place: Tag 05J9, lemma-flat-descend-pure, proof of (1) by lifting an elementary-etale impurity.

proof.text: Let $b:X_{T_1}\to X_T$ be the projection. Continuity gives $b(\overline{\{\xi_1\}})\subseteq\overline{\{\xi\}}$. If a point $z$ of this closure lay in $(X_{T_1})_{t_1}$, then $b(z)$ would lie in $(X_T)_t$, contradicting step 1. Thus the closure is disjoint from that fibre. Together with step 6, $t_1'\leadsto t_1$, and the elementary etale neighbourhood of step 2, these are exactly the data of an impurity of $F_Y$ above $s'$. This contradicts the assumed purity along $Y_{s'}$. Therefore $F$ is pure along $X_s$.
